name: LVL beam 2.0E
description: Laminated veneer lumber, 2.0E grade, in 1 3/4in plies: headers and beams longer than sawn lumber can span. Generic values from a typical manufacturer; size a real beam from that manufacturer's tables.
source: Boise Cascade Versa-Lam 2.1E 3100 Product Guide, Allowable Stress Values (ICC-ES ESR-1040): E 2,000,000 psi (apparent), Fb 3100 psi at 12in depth (× (12/d)^(1/9)), Fv 285, Ft 2150, Fc 3000, Fc⊥ 750 psi (edgewise); density 41.6 pcf from the published 5.7 plf for 1 3/4 × 11 1/4

name: Glulam beam 24F-V4 (Douglas fir)
description: Glued-laminated Douglas fir beam, stress class 24F-V4 (unbalanced: tension face down). Values are for bending about the strong axis, unadjusted.
source: ANSI 117-2020 Table A1-Expanded and APA PR-L313 (matching NDS Supplement Table 5A), 24F-V4 DF/DF: Fbx+ 2400 (Fbx− 1850), Ft 1100, Fvx 265, Fc⊥x 650, Fc 1650, Ex 1,800,000 psi; G 0.50; density ≈ 1000·G × 1.12 ÷ 1.06 at about 12% moisture, G from NDS 2018 Table 12.3.3A

name: Wood I-joist (generic)
description: Prefabricated wood I-joist: LVL or sawn flanges on an OSB web. Structural values are for the flange material only, a generic approximation; a real joist's capacity comes from the manufacturer's span table.
source: Generic: I-joist flanges are LVL (e.g. Weyerhaeuser TJI, ICC-ES ESR-1153 §3.2.1), so the flange material takes the Versa-Lam 2.1E 3100 values (ESR-1040); no generic I-joist values are published. Dimensions typical of a TJI 210 (2 1/16in flange, 1 1/4–1 3/8in deep, 3/8in OSB web; ESR-1153 Table 1)
